queries.query: Research whether the langgraph project is production-ready. Include GitHub releases, issues, and license evidence.
Write a literature review of Self-RAG, IRCoT, ReAct, and STORM for building a research agent. Include papers, code, limitations, and open questions.
Verify the claim that a graph-based retrieval system beats a flat one. Find supporting and contradicting evidence.
Compare three open research agent frameworks for a build-vs-adopt decision, with sources.
I uploaded a whitepaper. Summarize it and check whether its claims are still current using web sources.
Audit this GitHub repo for maintenance risk, security advisories, release history, docs/source mismatch, and license risk.
Produce a cited report on whether this benchmark result has replication failures or data contamination concerns.
Deep research: is this vendor's API suitable for production? Include official docs, changelog, the GitHub SDK, incidents, and competing views.
Is library X still current? Check the latest release notes and cite the changelog entry that confirms feature Y.
Here is our design document with performance numbers in it. Check the numbers against the public benchmarks and tell me which ones hold up.
Summarize this research paper in five bullets, without using external sources: Self-RAG proposes learning to retrieve, generate, and critique through self-reflection.
What is a literature review, and what sections does one usually have?
Find me papers about retrieval-augmented generation. Just a list of titles and links.
Translate this paragraph into Chinese: "Our research team publishes every paper in an open repository."
Brainstorm names for my research newsletter.
Chat casually with me about why research is hard.
Rewrite this summary so it reads better. Keep every fact as it is: "The team completed the migration in March and reduced latency by 20 percent."
Fix the grammar in this README sentence about the research pipeline.
What does RAG stand for?
Based only on this document, extract the abstract and the methods section: "We propose a graph-based retrieval system that preserves document relationships for multi-hop question answering."
I need to decide between two vector databases for our retrieval service. Compare them with sources and give me a recommendation.
Summarize what the published research on long-context models says about retrieval quality, with citations.
Our team claims the new orchestrator handles ten thousand requests per second. Verify that claim with evidence.
What is the difference between a preprint and a peer-reviewed paper?
List the ten most recent papers on retrieval-augmented generation, newest first.
Rewrite this paragraph about our research process so it reads better: "We surveyed the team, ran three interviews, and wrote up the findings in the usual way."
